Subject: Deployment mode & pricing - Acme / Redwood

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps: 

Call summary:
- Primary workload: customer support assistant + knowledge base search (low-latency responses, ~60% production inference).
- Expected steady-state QPS: ~30 requests/sec during business hours (peak ~80 rps), average payload ~400 tokens in, ~60 tokens out.
- Data sensitivity: must be inside Acme VPC for production (PII + contractual requirements).
- SLA: low latency (~100-200ms p50 for short completions) and predictable monthly spend.

Deployment modes discussed:
1) Hosted API (Redwood hosted): fastest to launch, per-token pricing, built-in model catalog. Good if you can accept data transit and our SOC2 controls.
2) Dedicated (reserved capacity): reserved GPU pools, monthly commit, predictable throughput and cost-per-token improvements for steady high QPS.
3) Private (VPC/on-prem): customer-managed networking and keys (KMS/HSM), ideal for regulated data — higher base platform fee + provisioning lead time.

Next steps I committed to:
- Share a simple cost model (per-token vs reserved capacity) for the usage profile you shared (attached: pricing_model.xlsx).
- Clarify network/security assumptions for Private VPC (who owns the VPC, egress rules).
- Schedule a follow-up to walk through the cost scenarios and recommended deployment.

Can you confirm the monthly average tokens in/out and whether you plan to keep models warm (hot-start) 24x5? That will materially affect the Reserved vs Per-token economics.

Thanks — talk soon.

—Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Alice —

Great questions — answers inline and next steps below.

Private VPC: yes, Private has a one-time onboarding fee (in the SOW) plus a platform subscription for private control plane; I'll include the draft SOW. Lead time is typically 4-6 weeks for VPC + keys provisioning if there are no additional networking constraints.

Reserved capacity billing: reserved capacity is a monthly commit for GPU slots (billed as a capacity commitment). Overage is allowed and billed at a defined committed overage rate that is lower than Hosted per-token prices; the blended cost depends on utilization. I'll have Marissa run a utilization-based cost model for your 12M/1.8M token profile showing: Hosted per-token, Dedicated reserved (3 commit tiers), and Private (platform + reserved).

I'll loop in Marissa and Neha from pricing to build the tailored model and the SOW draft. Can you confirm the 12M/1.8M monthly token numbers and whether you want a 12- or 24-month commit comparison?

Proposed follow-up: 45-minute call next Tuesday, Jun 22, 10:00 AM PT to walk the model?

Thanks,
Aditya

Thanks Aditya — attaching the initial deliverables.

High-level recommendation (one-pager):
- Pilot: Hosted API for a 3-month pilot to validate models and latency with reduced setup time and no upfront platform fee. 
- Production: Private VPC if Acme mandates in-contract VPC hosting (we recommend Private for production due to data residency). If Acme prefers lower capital, Dedicated (reserved) is the middle ground — lower unit cost at steady utilization but needs capacity commit and monitoring.

Numbers: see Acme_cost_model_v1.xlsx (tabs: inputs, hosted_vs_reserved, private_tco, assumptions). Key callouts:
- For the 12M/1.8M tokens profile, Dedicated reserved (medium commit) yields ~35% cost savings vs Hosted per-token at 70% utilization.
- Private adds a predictable platform fee (~$12k/month) plus slightly lower per-token execution cost vs Dedicated due to our negotiated infra pricing, but with a 4–6 week provisioning window and higher initial SOW.

Attached: Acme_cost_model_v1.xlsx, SOW_Acme_Redwood_draft.pdf

Notes on assumptions included in workbook. Happy to refine once Acme confirms commit length (12 vs 24 months).
